effect: Relaxation completes the cycle: ATP-powered pumps return calcium to storage, the grip sites are covered, and pulling stops.
reaction: It was useful to see that relaxation also requires ATP and that an outside pull is shown returning the fibre to its relaxed pose.

mostWorthwhile.text: The calcium-triggered pull was the most worthwhile moment: it connected a cellular signal to movement and showed that filaments slide rather than shorten.

leastWorthwhile.text: The scaffold and filament-fitting steps felt repetitive because each had only one offered combination and neither yet showed movement.

surprise.text: ATP helping myosin let go and reset, and also powering calcium pumps during relaxation, broadened my understanding of its role.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although combining the transporter-bearing cell with muscle fibre structures was more of an assembly step than an explanation of how those parts relate.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how this fibre's pull becomes coordinated movement at the tissue and body-system scale, although I would hope for more meaningful choices along the way.
